| \# | Piece | Length | What it is | Due |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 1 | **Reverse outline** | 1 page | Take an assigned published paper and reconstruct its outline: one topic sentence per paragraph, in order, in your own words. Then say in three lines what the argument actually is. | Meeting 9 --- Oct 21 (week 9)\* |
| 2 | **Reverse outline and repair** | 1 page | A badly organised passage. Give its real outline, then the outline it should have had, and say what moved and why. | Meeting 10 --- Oct 28 (week 10) |
| 3 | **Plain-language summary** | 1 page | Your project explained to a decision-maker who is not an economist. No jargon, no hedging, and the 'so what' in the first sentence. | Meeting 12 --- Nov 11 (week 12) |
| 4 | **Referee report** | 2 pages | A structured critique of another team's proposal outline, on the template used in class. You get theirs after meeting 13, and they get yours — so the critique arrives while there is still time to act on it. | Meeting 14 --- Dec 2 (week 15) |
